candidates.structural_interaction: Reach meeting reach cross-polarity — growth competing with growth
candidates.k2_overview: Your Wood moves as the Rival: growth that races the grove. Another’s success reads to you as proof of reachable height, and it pulls you upward faster than any plan. You share ground generously and compete on it constantly. Handled well, that doubles every harvest. Handled loosely, the roots start strangling.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy feeds on contest and outdoor motion, and sours in idle shade.

k2_domain_readings.Rivalry: Your rivalries are growth spurts: every worthy competitor adds a ring. Keep them seasonal rather than permanent. A race that never ends stops being training and becomes a root war.
k2_domain_readings.Shared stakes: You pool naturally: gardens, ventures, family plots tended together. Write down whose branch is whose before the fruit comes in. Shared soil grows the most and disputes the hardest.
k2_domain_readings.Boldness: Your daring is springlike: sudden reach toward light others have not noticed yet. Trust it early in ventures and slow it near contracts. Green wood bends into bad deals when the sun is exciting.

catalyst.define: Running thin, your reserve is shallow and comes in quick bursts. The people around you are where the rest of your reach comes from.

angles.drive: You go first, with the plan half done and the vote not in. Waiting your turn feels like losing, since the opening is worth more to you than certainty. Others find their nerve by watching you move.
angles.cost_self: Where the signal has not come, you have already gone. Being the one who moved counts for more than being the one who was ready. You take the first hit alone, every time.
angles.cost_others: Plan or no plan, you go first and let the rest catch up. Moving matters more than agreeing, and that puts your people a step behind their own decision. Your lead gives slower friends a path already cut.

angles.drive: A race wakes you up like nothing else. Having someone just ahead is your best fuel, since a pace you can see beats one you must invent. What you want is a rival worth keeping up with.
angles.cost_self: Racing brings out your best and spends most of it. Being ahead feels better than being rested, and that comes out of a reserve that was never deep. Your body runs on empty for days after each finish line.
angles.cost_others: You turn shared things into a race. Moving counts for more with you than winning, and that keeps the people beside you in motion long after their finish. Your friends get very few slow afternoons in your company.

angles.drive: Given the choice, you put the stakes in a shared pot. Being in it together makes a risk worth taking, since a bet carried alone weighs more than one split. Your partners never face a bad loss by themselves.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a venture needs a partner, you have already said yes. Going in together feels safer, and you would rather split a win than keep it whole. Half of every good year of yours belongs to someone else.
angles.cost_others: Your bets carry other people's names. You would rather share the risk than own the call, and that puts their money where your nerve is. Their savings rise and fall with your choices.

friction.define: Running over, the reach outgrows its roots. Falling behind is what you dread, and each new push costs ground the last one won.

angles.drive: You size every bet past what the moment asks. More drive sits in you than one plan can use, and the extra goes into the stake instead of the base under it. You fund next year's bet with the money this year needed.
angles.cost_self: Where a smaller bet would hold, you put down the big one. Playing small feels worse than losing, and you take the big risk ahead of sure footing. You lose real money on bets you never needed to make.
angles.cost_others: Your biggest bets land on other people too. Going big matters more than going safe, and that puts the shared money at your size of risk. You risk their savings along with your own whenever you bet too big.

angles.drive: Finished, you look for the next race before the last cools. Staying put feels like being passed, and there is more go in you than a finish uses. You race the next one instead of keeping the win, and the win was the point.
angles.cost_self: Racing without a finish is the shape of your effort. You keep going past where rest would pay rather than let anyone pass you. You trade each win for another race and never take the rest you earned.
angles.cost_others: Win or lose, you keep racing people who stopped a while ago. Staying ahead matters more than staying close, and that turns a friend into someone to beat. You take from them, by racing someone who stopped, the ease of just being with you.

angles.drive: Spending from the shared pot comes easier to you than spending from your own. Your drive runs past what the budget covers, and the shared money is the nearest way across. For the sake of moving, you let the pot pay for your speed.
angles.cost_self: You spend what is shared like your own nerve, fast and ahead of the count. Moving matters more than owing, and that is a difference the money remembers. You never get to keep what you spend there, and the owing stays with you.
angles.cost_others: Ahead of asking, you spend what was pooled and settle the split later. Keeping things moving counts for more than a fair split, and that puts their savings behind your speed. Each time you spend the shared money, you spend their say in it too.

edge.lead: Wood runs through your wealth, your social life and your career. It is the win that feels bigger once it is split in half, the lift you get when a friend pulls ahead, and the first move at work you make before anyone agrees.
